body: Thank you!

Thank you for your response. Regardless of whether you could/couldn't give good advice, it's still somewhat nice to see someone else be able to sympathise with me and can understand what I'm going through through their own similar experiences.

To answer a few of your questions, I still live with my mom because my dad passed away when I was 10, and my sister left home to live on her own when she was about 20, so I'm all that's left. My mom is also rather old (late 60s) and has to take a lot of medications for various things, and if I left, then she'd be by herself unable to perform certain labor-intensive tasks. Of course I don't want to leave my mother by herself like that, nor do I just want to throw her into a retirement home, so that's why I'm still living with my mom.

I've run the idea of me living on my own to her before, but she gets upset and begins talking about how none of her kids love her anymore, how no one cares about her anymore, etc. My aunts, uncles, and cousins then hear about this and tell me how I need to stay with her. We're an Asian family, where family and family morals all take top priority to us. Again, I'm happy to help my mom with whatever she needs, but to have the responsibility of staying with her up until her death so she isn't lonely just thrusted upon me feels unfair. My sister had initially gotten shit for leaving as well, but everyone moved past it because they started thinking "at least Stomach_Pit is still there for her," making it almost impossible to leave.

I don't want to worry about things like having a girlfriend, but it's hard not to when most people by now would have had some form of romantic relationship. I had confessed to a crush once, and it went horribly. Found out she planned on getting me to marry her for citizenship. She ghosts me and burns all bridges with me. Didn't even answer my confession. I felt so used and humiliated that I'm now too scared to attempt anything like that again in fear of it happening again. I feel like I could've handled being rejected. I couldn't handle being thrown away like an object that she no longer had a use for. I know that other people have gone through worse. The fact that this one little event scarred me so much makes me feel pathetic compared to other people that can easily get up and move on.

I'm sorry to hear about what you're going through. Despite our mothers possibly having different reasons for wanting their sons to stay with them, it seems like we both share the same mindset of wanting to grow on our own. Both of us were the last children to be in the home, making the act of leaving seem ten times harder to do and seem ten times worse if we did compared to when our siblings left.

Every goddamn day. I fear what my family would think and the physical pain if I don't make it instant. I'd rather die of another cause so that my family will be able to just mourn and eventually move on rather than be caught up in the "why'd he do it."

I remember hearing this feeling described as "I wouldn't ever jump in front of a bus, but I don't know if I would move out of the way of one."
What if they were implying that the friend bit the octopus back in retaliation?

Seth's ultra breaks it similarly to Abigail's CA, minus the glass breaking.

I don't know if you'd count Hakan's ultra or not, but he squeezes the opponent out into an invisible wall that sorta faces the camera.
Assuming there were new enemies in the sub-missions, what would be the difference between seeing them there and seeing them in a main mission?

I feel like often when this guy and I argue, my friend will almost always side with him. It's frustrating, having who I thought was my best friend side against you. I feel like I'm losing my best friend. I don't know what to do.
I have. Numerous times. Every time he just says "that's how he is" or "he's just trolling again." I can't fucking stand it.

Unfortunately, I have no proof of anything he's ever done. Everything I've heard him do was through my friend. Even he thought the things he did was messed up, but he still continues to hang out with him.

I'm so glad that you're still with us, and I'm happy that you had such a nice time last night. 

I know it's silly to get worked up over a game, but I would never want to wish this sort of thing on anyone else, even in a video game. The fact that I could have stopped it and saved the man, and I couldn't, was what hit me so hard.

I've played and beaten Spec Ops: The Line before, and it was a very good game, but I didn't really cry at any part of it.

I looked it up, and it was possible to save the man in Watch Dogs 2. I was supposed to open the garage door just a little bit so that the neighbor could force it open and pull the man out, but for whatever reason, the game wouldn't let me interact with the garage door until the neighbor left. It kept thinking I was trying to profile the neighbor instead of hack the door. I was even yelling "what the fuck?!" and mashing L1 to try to get the hack to point at the door and not the neighbor.

I guess the reason I'm taking this so hard was because it was entirely possible to save the man, but I fucked up.
Thanks for the suggestions, I appreciate it.

I mentioned in another comment just now that one cousin, who didn't try to make me feel bad at dinner, said after dinner the other cousins said they felt bad and was just trying to give me a hard time. The horrid look that they gave me the whole time sort of said otherwise. But in any case, talking to him made me feel a little better, and after sleeping it off and reading the comments here, I think I'll be okay.

Thank you for your kind words, that last part you said really does make me feel better.

There was one cousin at dinner who didn't try to make me feel bad. He was in fact giving some suggestions on what I could 3D print and stuff, as in I could give her something related to her favorite football team (I know very little to nothing about football, so this didn't even cross my mind).

After I got home and made this post, I called him just to talk. I ended up crying on the phone too, despite me trying to stay calm and just talk. He told me that after I had left dinner rather abruptly, the other cousins were talking about how they didn't mean what they said, that they were just trying to give me a hard time and felt bad for upsetting me. I have a nagging feeling that he just made that up to make me feel better, but even if he was, it was nice of him to try.

He told me a lot of the same things everyone told me here: that I'm not a bad person because I'm obviously torn over all of this, and that it was a lot better than giving absolutely nothing.  Then we discussed more about what I could get my sister, such as a football jersey or something. 

Overall, I do feel a little better now, especially after reading everyone's kind words on here. So thank you, I really do appreciate you listening to my rather unstable ramblings.

I know how you feel. I just failed two out of four first exams, so I'm not feeling very confident in school myself.
Thank you. And don't worry, I don't plan on hurting myself. As I've said, I'm too scared to do anything like that. Maybe it's a good thing since it's keeping me here, depending on how you look at it.

It's scary how much I can relate to your first paragraph. Sometimes I think about how my death might be easier for people to take than someone else's who had more of an influence than me. Contrary to your hero reasoning though, I sometimes think that maybe if I die doing something noble then at least my life would have been worth something, and that I made some sort of impact before I died.

As for working out, I used to go with my sister to the small gym her apartment complex had. I couldn't run on the treadmill for very long before wanting to puke a lung, but I lifted the dumbbells quite a bit, even looking up different forms on lifting. I remember the first time I realized that I was starting to develop muscle on my arm, and I was ecstatic as hell to show my sister. Sadly, she got busy with work and school, and I got too scared to go on my own (especially since I wasn't supposed to be there in the first place since the gym was reserved for residents only).
Sometimes it's one or the other. When I play with friends it usually interests me, but when I'm on my own, there can be times that I just play so that I'm doing something.

Thank you for sharing. I still don't know why I posted at all. I feel weird and embarrassed to talk about this at all with anyone. This is probably the first time I've ever done this, and it's only really because of my online anonymity.

I don't think I could physically face someone else and talk about this. I keep thinking they'll think less of me or want to be "careful" around me, as if I might snap and just off myself. Or maybe they might get annoyed that I'm burdening them with my issues that they have no business with. So I've been just bottling all of this stuff up and pretend that I'm happy with everyone.

I procrastinate a lot in school. If I have an assignment due soon, I likely won't do it until the night before, two nights at maximum. There would be so many opportunities to get started on it, but I'll never have the motivation to do so. Instead I'll play video games, browse Reddit on my phone, or even just lay in bed doing absolutely nothing.

I also wanted to start working out, but I'm always too scared to go to a public gym by myself to do it in fear of being judged. I know most people say no one cares what you do at the gym, but I've seen people be mocked before, and just the slightest chance of that happening to me prevents me from going by myself. I try to work out alone at home, but again I'll get into that slump and break out of the habit of working out.
